title: Cool ASF

comments.author: syn_krown
comments.body:
https://hub.synkrown.workers.dev/?game=terrarium-tycoon

I made a live stream terrarium simulator game with procedurally generated insects, bugs, plants and lizards. 

It has a fake chat with fake users who tune in, comment of events happening in the terrarium, send you donations etc. The better your terraroum, the more viewers you will get, and the more money rolls in.

You can level up, and unlock a "Bug Lab", which you can put different critters in and combine them into a super critter. 

Sometimes pest bugs will enter the terrarium, so keep on top of that!

replies.author: ChillmanITB
replies.body: insane concept, really cool gameplay, hats off. creative!

replies.author: syn_krown
replies.body:
I appreciate you taking the time to check it out. I made it for a friend who loves insects. It was also a test to see how good AI is with assisted coding.

As impressed as I am with AI, I dont see how people are vibecoding full apps and games without programming knowledge. I have about 20 years of programming behind me and the amount of things I had to figure out myself... In saying that, maybe a lot of the "success" stories of vibecoding are more like adverts.

Using AI for coding is like having an exoskeleton imo. If you dont know how to lift a box, an exoskeleton is not going to fill that gap.

comments.author: MajoraGray
comments.body:
Basically I built a 2D Canvas based engine that makes heavy use of visibility occlusion using the players actual line of sight called DarkEngine.

Then proceeded to make 2 totally different games with it.

Dead Shelter is a shelter management/looter game (in a similar style to This War of Mine or Into The Dead: Outlr Darkest Days)

[Dead Shelter](https://deadshelter.pages.dev)

Arcadia is a single player top-down arena shooter combining gunplay with magical abilities (closest gameplay example would be Bullet Echo maybe?)

[Arcadia](https://arcadia-tds.pages.dev)
